newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway union warns of strike in oil sector.
newsitem.headline: Norway union warns of strike in oil sector.

text.p: The Norwegian Oil and Petrochemical Union (NOPEF) said on Thursday that 3,500 mainly oil service workers had been told of possible strike action beginning next Monday if negotiations between unions and employeers were not resolved over the weekend.
Employers were notified by Norway's Trade Union Confederation (LO) on Thursday of a possible strike, NOPEF spokesman Terje Johansen told Reuters.

On Wednesday LO walked out of negotiations with management over this year's wage settlements despite state mediation. The talks, with the employers' Confederation of Trade and Industry (NHO), are over retirement age and wage rises.

State appointed mediator Reidar Webster stepped in on Tuesday to try and solve the outstanding issues after initial negotiations collapsed on March 19. He has until midnight (2200 GMT) on Sunday to mediate a deal.
The parties are due to meet again on Friday.
A series of strikes hurting the offshore and manufacturing industries marred Norway's labour scene for a few months last year after state-led mediation failed to bring parties together in time.
This year's talks are supplementary only to the two-year central 1996 wage talks.
"The LO sent out strike warnings today. For us this will affect 3,500 offshore and onshore workers of which between 1,500 and 2,000 are oil service workers," NOPEF's Johansen said.
"This will not affect production immediately, that would take some time, but it will affect supplies and transport to and from the rigs and platforms, and catering," he said.
